ajv 6 comes with eslint inside @sap/cds-dk, a devDependency. `pnpm audit --prod` still lists it because @cap-js/postgres declares @sap/cds-dk as an optional peer that pnpm links from the admin's devDependencies; a production install has no cds-dk and the admin image never installs it (Trivy: no ajv 6 finding).

Reached only through download tooling that never runs at runtime: services/admin > sqlite3 > node-gyp > make-fetch-happen (builds the native addon at install time) and the admin devDependency cds-plugin-ui5 > @ui5/project > make-fetch-happen (UI5 build). No source file loads make-fetch-happen, node-gyp or http-cache-semantics; the max-stale disclosure needs a shared multi-user HTTP cache, which neither path is. It is in docker/pnpm-lock.yaml (sqlite3 dependency), so the reason is reachability, not absence.

No patched release exists (every version <=3.0.3 is affected). braces ships in no image: the gateway image was Trivy-clean once the unused root dependency http-proxy-middleware went, and the admin image since its node_modules comes from a production-only install (docker/admin.Dockerfile runtime-deps stage) instead of the build stage, which had carried jest, cpy, ui5-tooling-modules and @sap/hdi-deploy (each via micromatch). It is not in docker/pnpm-lock.yaml or npm-dist/sail-proxy/pnpm-lock.yaml. It stays in the development tree: `pnpm audit` reaches it through nodemon > chokidar (dev), and `pnpm audit --prod` through @cap-js/postgres > @sap/cds-dk > @sap/hdi-deploy > micromatch, because the lockfile resolves @cap-js/postgres optional peer @sap/cds-dk against the dev install; neither runs in a shipped server. The stack-exhaustion also needs attacker-controlled glob patterns. Verified 2026-10-06 with Trivy on rebuilt images and both audit passes.
